newsitem.title: USA: Tenneco says no gas cut due line problem.
newsitem.headline: Tenneco says no gas cut due line problem.

text.p: Tenneco Inc said Thursday it does not anticipate any natural gas supply disruptions to customers despite a minor problem on its BlueWater System, a gas gathering system offshore Louisiana.
"It's a non-event. We were having difficulty running the pig through the pipe on the BlueWater system," company spokeswoman Christine LeLaurin told Reuters.
A pig a device typically run through a pipeline to clean or inspect it.
She said the problem likely would be corrected "in the next couple of hours."
NYMEX natural gas futures for delivery at Henry Hub, Louisiana, rose sharply on market rumours that the line was blocked.

Traders said talk of the problem and uncertainty over the volume of gas that might be involved helped push the December NYMEX natgas contract to a session high of $2.80 per million British thermal units, up 15.5 cents from Wednesday's close.
The spot contract had since settled back a bit, and was trading at $2.780 as of 1414 EST.
-- H McCulloch, New York Power Desk + 1 212 859 1628
